newsitem.title: UK: London shares close higher, market remains nervous.
newsitem.headline: London shares close higher, market remains nervous.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE 100 ends higher but trading volumes remained
light as investors continued to worry about politics and
interest rates.
** FTSE near-term resistance pegged at 4,355, support 4,300.
** Oils, banks, pharmaceuticals bolster UK blue chips.
Turnover was again inflated by active trade in market newcomer Alliance & Leicester Plc, which made its debut on Monday.
Around 65 million Alliance shares changed hands, accounting for nearly 11 percent of the FTSE's total volume of about 610 million by 1530 GMT.
Declining issues pipped advancers by 48 to 47, with five FTSE 100 constituents unchanged.
Uncertainties about the timing and the size of the next UK interest rate hike continued to weigh on market sentiment, dealers said.
"The market has already discounted at least a 25 basis point hike next month. But if we get 50 basis points, there could be a bit of panic," another trader said.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who told BBC Radio on Monday there was no sign of consumer demand accelerating, has been resisting requests by the Bank of England to push up British rates, claiming that economic fundamentals do not warrant any fiscal tightening.
Clarke is like Nelson," one trader said. "He's turning a blind eye to the problem. We have a very fast moving service sector and rates will have to go up faster than people expect.

SmithKline Beecham Plc shot up 26-1/2p to 932-1/2, after the company hailed its underlying growth in sales and profits as "excellent", despite the strong pound, which had adversely impacted on overall earnings.
SmithKline reported an eight percent rise in Q1 profit despite a "dramatic" impact from sterling, which has risen over 20 percent against major European currencies since last summer.
Elsewhere in the sector, Glaxo Holdings Plc rose 13p to 11.63-1/2 stg, while Zeneca Plc jumped 27-1/2p to 18.67 stg.
Barclays Bank Plc was up 5p to 10.336-1/2 stg, after the company told its annual meeting it had made a good start to 1997, with an encouraging first quarter for its investment banking arm, BZW.
Royal Bank of Scotland Plc gained 8-1/2p to 552-1/2, while HSBC Holdings Plc added 4-1/2p to 15.43-1/2 stg.
Shares in Alliance & Leicester Plc, which made a sparkling market debut on Monday, fell 34p to 532-1/2 as some analysts suggested the shares may have been pushed up too sharply yesterday.
"I think the market got a bit ahead of itself yesterday," one analyst said. "But I wouldn't rule out a bounce in the next few days. You have to expect volatility as the market finds a fair value."
Recent strong quarterly earnings statements from U.S. oil companies lifted Shell Transport and Trading Plc 13p to 10.64-1/2 stg, while British Petroleum added 11p to 702-1/2.
Reckitt and Colman bounced 15-1/2p to 823 after NatWest Securities said it was advising clients to add to their Reckitt holdings.
Furniture maker DFS rose 16p to 548-1/2, after the company reported first-half pre-tax profits of 18.7 million stg, ahead of expectations, and said it was confident of continued growth and success.
Technical analysts said the FTSE is likely to encounter near-term resistance at the 4,355 level followed by 4,365-70, with support seen at 4,317 then 4,300.
--Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
